name: Four Seasons Hotel Baku
insider_take: Where Caspian elegance meets fire-touched landscapes in Azerbaijan's captivating capital.
whats_special: This luxury haven sits in the heart of Baku's UNESCO-listed Old City, where ancient Zoroastrian fire temples once burned eternal flames. The hotel offers stunning views of the Caspian Sea - the world's largest lake - and the city's iconic Flame Towers that illuminate the skyline like modern fire altars, paying homage to Azerbaijan's nickname "Land of Fire."
pro_tip: Visit during late spring when Baku's famous mud volcanoes are most active - over half of the world's mud volcanoes are found in Azerbaijan, creating an otherworldly landscape just outside the city.
dont_miss: The nearby Maiden Tower's mysterious architecture (no one knows its original purpose), and Baku's incredible oil heritage - this city was producing 50% of the world's oil supply in 1901, making it richer than Paris at the time. The contrast between ancient Shirvanshah's Palace and ultra-modern Heydar Aliyev Center creates an unforgettable architectural journey.
pros: Prime waterfront location on Caspian Sea with stunning views
Luxury amenities including world-class spa and rooftop pool
Exceptional Four Seasons service standards and concierge
Modern sophisticated design with local Azerbaijani cultural elements
cons: Limited nearby dining options outside hotel
